body:
MRP: 

[Archive.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21697185/Archive.zip)

The jump does not go into the abort state, even though the variable is true.
Note: If you change the transition priority from 2 to 0, then the transition works.

I have reproduced this issue in 4.5-stable. System information: `Godot v4.5.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL ES 3/ANGLE (Compatibility) - ANGLE (Intel, Intel(R) HD Graphics 5500 (0x00001616) Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11-20.19.15.5171) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i3-5005U CPU @ 2.00GHz (4 threads) - 7.92 GiB memory`

I can reproduce this on 4.7.2.stable, and the same code path is on current master.

Cause: `AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback::_find_next()` keeps only the single best-priority transition among those whose advance condition passes. If that one is `SWITCH_MODE_AT_END` and the current state has not reached its end yet, `_can_transition_to_next()` rejects it, and the other outgoing transitions (like the immediate one whose condition is true) are never evaluated. That is also why lowering the priority number of the immediate transition works around it.

I'd like to work on a fix, so I'm claiming this. Please let me know if someone is already on it.

So, in short, the issue you said is that when evaluating them in order of priority, if both AtEnd (high priority) and Immediate (low priority) are available for transition, "waiting for AtEnd" takes precedence over the Immediate transition.

Given that this behavior hasn't been changed so far, I'm not sure if we should change it.

The problem with changing this behavior in particular is that, while it is currently possible to avoid the pointed-out issue by changing the priority, making this change would make it impossible to perform the original behavior of "waiting for high-priority AtEnd".

Even if we do change it, I believe we'll have to make it optional (like old behavior becomes `leagcy_mode`?), otherwise it will break old projects. Or, alternatively, we should add a property like `halt` to AtEnd StateMachineTransition class that halts the search during priority exploration, thereby maintaining the current behavior.

@SaracenOne @lyuma As one of the main contributors to StateMachine, how do you think?
